references.text: The description of how the courtyard was actually built, as a fulfillment of the instructions given in Exodus 27:9.
Use of fine twisted linen (שֵׁשׁ מָשְׁזָר) in the construction of the tabernacle, the same material used for the hangings of the courtyard.
Moses sets up the courtyard around the tabernacle as the completion of God's command.
Summary of the dimensions of the courtyard, confirming the one hundred cubits in length mentioned in verse 9.
Solomon's temple also had an inner court, showing continuity in sanctuary design from the tabernacle.
Ezekiel's vision of the temple's court, reflecting the original pattern from the tabernacle's courtyard.
The execution of the command: The source gives the instruction for the south side, while this verse confirms it was carried out exactly as specified.
The distinction between the side hangings and the gate hanging: The source describes the wall, while this verse describes the entrance to the same area.
Overall perspective: Confirms that all the hangings around the entire area followed the standard from the source.
Comparison of materials: Connects the gate hanging directly to the hangings described in the source to show unity in design.
